routes.description: Establish that contingency, a finite cosmic past, life-permitting fine-tuning, objective morality, and the historical case for Jesus's resurrection collectively raise the probability of God's existence.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the cited facts are sufficiently established, are more expected or better explained given theism than its relevant alternatives, and cumulatively support the motion's evidentiary threshold.

motionBridge.description: The motion is satisfied if the cumulative considerations make God's existence more probable than it would otherwise be.

centralBridges.description: Contingent reality and a universe with a finite past must warrant inference to a necessary, transcendent causal ground.
Life-permitting constants and initial conditions must be better explained by design than by necessity, chance, or multiverse selection.
Objective moral values and duties must exist and require an ontological foundation supplied by God's necessary moral nature.
The relevant historical facts concerning Jesus must be established and better explained by divine resurrection than by naturalistic alternatives.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Philosophical, moral, historical, and scientific considerations must be admissible within a probability-raising conception of evidence.
The several independent considerations must retain material cumulative force even if no individual consideration proves theism by itself.

routes.description: Show that the affirmative considerations are unsupported, underdetermined, or more plausibly addressed through empirical naturalism, so they do not supply adequate evidence for a divine cause or the Christian God.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the affirmative fails to justify its probability assignments or if natural models, explanatory uncertainty, secular morality, and ordinary historical explanations prevent the cited facts from discriminating in favor of God.

motionBridge.description: The motion is not established unless the affirmative supplies testable or otherwise warranted evidence that favors God over relevant natural alternatives.

centralBridges.description: Quantum-gravity, multiverse, or other physical possibilities must block the inference from contingency or cosmic beginnings to a uniquely divine cause.
Dynamical explanations and observer selection must make apparent fine-tuning insufficient to distinguish purposive design from natural cosmology.
Moral truth or understanding must remain intelligible without divine grounding, or the proposed divine foundation must face an unresolved arbitrariness problem.
Human error, illusion, imagination, or intervention must remain more plausible than resurrection as explanations of the reported historical claims.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Claims about divine evidence must meet a defensible empirical or probabilistic standard rather than rest on intuition or unquantified priors.
Present explanatory ignorance must remain a reason for continued investigation rather than an evidential inference to supernatural agency.

sections.title: Evidential Standards and the Cumulative Inference
sections.rationale: The parties dispute what qualifies as evidence, how probability-raising claims are warranted, where the burden lies, and whether several distinct considerations can jointly support the motion.

sections.title: Contingency and the Necessary Explanatory Ground
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether contingent reality requires an external necessary explanation and whether God has any justified advantage over a necessary or eternal natural terminus.

sections.title: Cosmic Beginning, Infinity, and Transcendent Causation
sections.rationale: The finite-past argument depends on philosophical claims about actual infinity, scientific claims about cosmic boundaries, and the inference from a beginning to a transcendent cause.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning, Design, and Multiverse Selection
sections.rationale: This section addresses whether life-permitting conditions favor purposive design or are better treated through dynamics, varied universes, observer selection, and unresolved physical theory.

sections.title: Moral Objectivity and Divine Grounding
sections.rationale: The moral argument requires both objective values or duties and a uniquely divine ontology, while the opposing route contests that dependence through rational, biological, and arbitrariness-based alternatives.

sections.title: Resurrection and Competing Historical Explanations
sections.rationale: The historical pillar turns on the status of the alleged facts, their connection to God's existence, and the comparative plausibility of resurrection against ordinary human explanations.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: Facts concerning the universe, morality, and history collectively raise the probability that God exists.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: The existence of contingent beings is best explained by a necessarily existing transcendent cause identified as God.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: The universe began to exist and therefore has a transcendent cause beyond space and time, best identified as God.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: The universe's life-permitting fine-tuning is better explained by design than by physical necessity or chance.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Objective moral values and duties exist, and their existence entails God because atheism cannot ground their objectivity.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: The empty tomb, postmortem appearances, and disciples' transformed belief are best explained by Jesus's resurrection, which entails God.

chunk-002:c002-04.proposition: Mathematical treatments of infinity and quantum-vacuum cosmology do not defeat the evidence that the universe and its physical state began.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-01.proposition: A many-worlds hypothesis does not explain embodied interactive observers and instead relocates fine-tuning to the laws governing the multiverse.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-02.proposition: Divine commands necessarily express God's compassionate, just, and fair character, while naturalism lacks a foundation for objective moral duties and values.

chunk-004:c004-05.proposition: Widely accepted historical facts surrounding Jesus are best explained by resurrection because rival naturalistic accounts fail standard explanatory criteria.

chunk-004:c004-07.proposition: Explanatory inquiry stops non-arbitrarily with God because contingent things require external causes whereas God exists necessarily by his own nature.

chunk-004:c004-09.proposition: Restricting rational evidence to scientific proof is self-defeating, while theism jointly explains moral, philosophical, historical, and scientific facts.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Craig bears the affirmative burden of supplying recognizable empirical evidence for God, while Krauss need not disprove God's existence.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: An infinitely powerful divine intelligence is an extraordinary claim requiring correspondingly extraordinary evidence, which ordinary probability assertions do not by themselves supply.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: Classical intuitions about the absurdity of infinity cannot override mathematics and empirically successful physics, both of which consistently employ infinite quantities.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Contingency and presently unexplained causal processes do not support God, because unknown explanations invite investigation and may ultimately prove entirely physical.

chunk-002:c002-01.proposition: Quantum gravity, inflation, and a potentially eternal multiverse provide natural models in which our universe can arise spontaneously without a relevant divine first cause.

chunk-002:c002-02.proposition: If an act would remain wrong despite divine approval, moral truth constrains God's choices and therefore neither originates in God nor gains explanatory grounding from God.

chunk-002:c002-08.proposition: Quantum-gravitational origins, universes with varying laws, and observer selection provide physical explanations for apparent fine-tuning without supernatural imposition.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: Rationality, evolution, biology, and continued investigation can explain moral understanding and conduct without belief in or dependence upon God.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: Known dynamics explain some alleged fine-tuning, while the unexplained vacuum-energy value is not shown to be life-necessary and does not evidence competent purposive design.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-09.proposition: Reports of Jesus's resurrection are more plausibly attributable to mistaken human testimony than to a miraculous event and therefore do not provide adequate evidence for God.

chunk-004:c004-04.proposition: Human error, imagination, illusion, or deliberate intervention are more plausible explanations of resurrection claims than an extraordinary supernatural resurrection.

chunk-004:c004-08.proposition: Defining God as the necessary explanatory terminus has no demonstrated advantage over an eternal multiverse, which can serve as a natural terminus and is physically motivated.
